HIGHLIGHTS 
 
PHOTO EXPERIENCE LTD. WINS THE DIGITAL AWARD 
AT THE 2026 NATIONAL ENTERPRISE AWARDS

National Enterprise Awards, presented at the Mansion House

OFFICIAL OPENING OF BÓTHAR NA LAOCHRA

na Laochra was officially opened on 8 June 2026 by the

presence of Cllr. John Leahy, Cathaoirleach of Offaly 
County Council, and Cllr. Hugh Egan, Cathaoirleach of

LIBRARY &ARTS BASE

Edenderry Community Library and Arts Base on 18 June, a 
landmark town centre regeneration project, with Minister for Rural 
and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, Dara Calleary 
TD, in attendance

Minister of State for Planning and Local Government, John 
Cummins TD, visited Beechwood Court, Daingean, on 
Friday 26 June, for a site visit to view the strong progress 
made on this Age Friendly housing development, which is 
now approaching completion.

EDENDERRY BUSINESS ENGAGEMENT 
LEO Offaly promoted 2026 funding opportunities and 
supports through a Business Advice Clinic held in 
Edenderry Town Hall on 24th of June. The initiative 
encouraged local businesses at all stages to engage with 
advisors for tailored guidance on grants, training, and 
other supports. This outreach aimed to increase 
awareness, drive uptake of LEO services, and support 
business growth in the Edenderry area. 
 
 
 
NATIONAL WOMEN’S ENTERPRISE DAY 2026 – SAVE THE DATE 
National Women’s Enterprise Day, is taking place on the 15th of 
October 2026 and is marking its 20th anniversary. The campaign 
aims to engage and inspire women at all stages of business 
through a series of regional and national events. 
The initiative will showcase female entrepreneurs, provide 
practical advice, and highlight available supports.

SUPPORTING OPPORTUNITY AT THE OFFALY JOB FAIR 
LEO Offaly was delighted to attend and be a sponsor 
of the Offaly Job Fair 2026, a fantastic event 
showcasing the wide range of businesses and 
employment opportunities across the Midlands. 
It was great to meet so many attendees on the day, all 
keen to connect with employers, explore career 
options and learn more about the exciting work 
happening within local organisations. The atmosphere 
was vibrant and positive, with strong engagement from 
both exhibitors and visitors. 
 
 
LUNCH AND LEARN - KILCORMAC 
We hosted a Lunch & Learn event at Kilcormac KDA, 
Work Well Hub, bringing together local businesses to 
explore the wide range of supports available from LEO 
Offaly. 
The session provided valuable insights into supports 
such as grant aid, mentoring and training, along with 
programmes including Green for Business, Lean for 
Business and Digital for Business. It was great to see 
such strong engagement from attendees keen to learn 
how they can grow and develop their businesses in 
Offaly. 
 
 
RHODE GREEN ENERGY PARK DEVELOPMENT 
Offaly County Council welcomed the announcement of a major partnership investment 
by Google and Energy Dome to develop a 23 MW/200 MWh energy storage facility at 
Rhode Green Energy Park. This landmark project, a first for Ireland, represents a 
significant step in the development and repurposing of the park into a centre for green 
energy innovations and research.  
The project which will be developed by local company Lumcloon Energy, reinforces 
Offaly’s position as a key hub for renewable energy infrastructure and highlights Rhode 
Green Energy park’s ability to attract world class technology and international 
collaborations to the Midlands.  North Offaly Development Fund, and Offaly County 
Council’s Economic Development section collaborated tirelessly bringing together the 
many stakeholders of this project over the past two years, ensuring the investment 
would be realised in Offaly.

ROADS 
R441 MONASTERORIS ROAD WIDENING SCHEME – APPROVAL TO PROCEED TO 
TENDER 
The construction of the R441 Monasteroris Road Widening Scheme is progressing 
under the Department of Transport’s Specific Improvement Grant Programme, having 
received approval to proceed to tender. 
The scheme includes the widening of approximately 270 metres of the existing 
roadway. The design also includes the provision of 2.2 metre footpaths on both sides 
and a 1.5 metre cycle track, significantly enhancing accessibility and improving safety 
for pedestrians and cyclists. 
The scheme will tie in with the Edenderry Inner Relief Road, thereby improving network 
connectivity and facilitating smoother traffic flow in the area. 
Offaly County Council will invite suitably qualified contractors to submit tenders for the 
execution of the works. 
 
OFFALY HOSPICE SPECIALIST PALLIATIVE CARE UNIT 
Commencement of the Part 8 planning process for the proposed development of a 
new Midlands Specialist Palliative Care Unit on a greenfield site accessible from Arden 
Lane, Tullamore. 
Road infrastructure works include upgrades to a portion of Arden Lane to provide a 
two-way carriageway with footpaths, public lighting, and utility connections.  The Part 8 
process is ongoing. 
 
HOUSING INFRASTRUCTURE AND INVESTMENT FUND 
Approval of the three HIIF-funded schemes represents a significant advancement from 
a roads and infrastructure perspective, enabling the delivery of critical transport and 
utility networks to support planned housing growth in Tullamore and Birr.  
The Clonminch scheme in Tullamore centres on the construction of a 1 km link road 
alongside water and wastewater infrastructure, unlocking substantial residential 
capacity while integrating with ongoing ESB grid upgrades and planned Uisce Éireann 
network expansion.  
In Birr, the Rectory Fields scheme enhances connectivity through the provision of a link 
road and active travel infrastructure within the town centre, strengthening the existing

OFFICIAL OPENING OF BÓTHAR NA LAOCHRA  
The Birr North Distruibutor Road, now known as Bóthar na Laochra was officially 
opened on 8 June 2026 by the Minister for Transport, Darragh O’Brien TD, in the 
presence of Cllr. John Leahy, Cathaoirleach of Offaly County Council, and Cllr. Hugh 
Egan, Cathaoirleach of Birr Municipal District. The approximately €3 million project, 
funded by the Department of Transport, forms a key part of the Birr Distributor Road 
network, providing a strategic link between the R439 Banagher Road and the N52 
Tullamore Road. The scheme enhances connectivity, improves road safety, supports 
active travel, reduces congestion in Birr town centre, and unlocks opportunities for 
future residential and economic development. It also delivers significant benefits for 
local schools, businesses and tourism, reflecting Offaly County Council’s commitment 
to sustainable infrastructure investment and collaborative project delivery.

FORWARD PLANNING 
PROPOSED VARIATION:  
The closing date for receipt of submissions on the proposed Variation no. 1 of the Offaly 
County Development Plan 2021-2027 was 16th June 2026.  The reason for the proposed 
variation is: 
 
(i) 
To provide increased housing growth requirements in alignment with the 
‘National Planning Framework Implementation: Housing Growth Requirement 
Guidelines’, published 29th July 2025, through the provision of additional ‘New 
Residential’ land use zonings. The proposed variation will provide for increased 
housing growth requirements which will extend beyond the lifetime of the 
current Development Plan i.e. up to 2030.  
(ii) 
Provision of ‘Open Space, Amenity and Recreation’ land use zoning on a site 
in Birr to reflect its established use as a sports and recreation ground. 
(iii) 
Provision of ‘Existing Residential’ land use zonings to provide for the rezoning 
of a site in Tullamore from ‘Enterprise and Employment’ zoning to ‘Existing 
Residential’ zoning and for the rezoning of lands from ‘Strategic Residential 
Reserve’ zoning to ‘Existing Residential’ zoning at Ferbane, reflecting their 
existing use as residential. 
(iv) 
Provision of ‘Business or Technology Park’ land use zoning of an identified 
strategic land bank in Tullamore to facilitate future economic development.  
(v) 
Provisions for ‘Peatland and Nature Corridors’ (Currently referred to as 
‘Wilderness Corridors’). The proposed Variation No. 1 proposes to update 
existing provisions on ‘Wilderness Corridors’, by way of amendments to 
objective BLO-28, Policy CAEP-38 and other associated text changes within the 
existing County Development Plan, in conjunction with mapping to give effect 
to ‘Peatland and Nature Corridors’ within the County. 
A Chief Executive’s Report on the 71 no. submissions will be circulated in July to the 
elected members for their consideration at the July Council Meeting.

The Council achieved: 
• 4 Excellent ratings 
• 9 Strong ratings 
• 2 Moderate ratings 
• 0 Limited ratings

environmental functions.

AREAS RATED EXCELLENT INCLUDED:

To promote this positive work by CAERW, this achievement shall be publicly promoted

These results reﬂect robust environmental governance, structured inspection planning,

Despite ongoing staﬃng and recruitment challenges, the assessment acknowledged

• 752 waste complaints investigated 
• 1,248 waste inspections 
• 679 illegal dumping investigations 
• 1,466 litter patrols

Two areas—Commercial Waste and Construction & Demolition Waste—received

• Strengthened reporting arrangements 
Overall, the LAPF assessment represents a positive outcome for Offaly County Council 
and provides a clear roadmap for continued improvement in 2026.

ENVIRONMENT AWARENESS / LITTER MANAGEMENT 
Offaly County Council successfully prosecuted an individual for illegal dumping at 
Cadamstown, Kinnitty. Mixed domestic waste was identified by Litter Warden Alan 
Conroy, and evidence recovered during investigation linked the waste to the defendant. 
A €150 Fixed Penalty Notice was issued but not paid within the statutory 21 days, 
resulting in legal proceedings under Section 32(1) of the Waste Management Act 1996. 
The case was heard at Tullamore District Court on 10 April 2026, where the defendant 
pleaded guilty. He informed Judge Coady that he had since engaged an authorised 
waste collector. The case was adjourned to 12 June 2026 to allow verification of this 
claim. The defendant was unable to provide proof, and Judge Coady imposed a €750 
fine. This success was highlighted by CAERW on social media where it gained positive 
momentum, highlighting an increasing intolerance to illegal dumping from the public.  
WASTE ENFORCEMENT – STONESTOWN ELV CASE  
Offaly County Council completed the remediation of an unauthorised End-of-Life 
Vehicle site at Stonestown, Cloghan. Over 100 ELVs and associated waste were 
removed following enforcement action, and a Section 14 Notice was fully complied 
with. The site has been restored to compliance, environmental risks have been 
eliminated, and proper storage and spill-response measures are now in place. This 
represents a successful enforcement outcome and a significant reduction in pollution 
risk. 
 
ANTI-DUMPING INITIATIVE 
Offaly County Council received €80,000 under the national Anti-Dumping Initiative 
(ADI) administered through the regional WERLA offices. The scheme supports projects 
aligned with the four ADI pillars: prevention, education, abatement, and enforcement. 
APPROVED PROJECTS 
Project 1 – Tackling Illegal Dumping at Bring Sites and Urban Areas (€50,000) 
This project targets persistent illegal dumping at bring centres, housing estates, back 
lanes, and other litter blackspots. Key components include: 
• Installation of CCTV 
• Education and awareness initiatives 
• Abatement measures to reduce recurring dumping

CLIMATE ACTION 
Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment, Darragh O’Brien TD, and Frank 
Curran, Chief Executive of Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council, launched the 
Climate Action Charter 2026 on behalf of the local government sector. The Charter sets 
out updated commitments to support an all-of-Government approach to climate action 
and builds upon the first Charter (2019), reflecting progress and changes in national 
climate policy. 
The Charter was formally signed by Cathaoirleach Cllr. John Leahy and Chief Executive 
Mr. Eoghan Ryan on behalf of Offaly County Council. The Council looks forward to 
working collaboratively with central government to deliver on these commitments. 
Local authorities remain a primary mechanism for climate action delivery, supported by 
national policy and funding structures. 
 
COMMUNITY CLIMATE ACTION PROGRAMME – PHASE 2. 
Phase 2 has progressed to the Grant Agreement stage. Contracts between Offaly County 
Council and the 20 participating community groups are scheduled for signing by 29 June 
2026. Once signed, projects may commence. All projects must be completed and fully 
drawn down by 29 September 2027.

attendance.

The ceremony signals the commencement of construction on this landmark town 
centre regeneration project at 33/34 JKL Street, the former Tesco Supermarket site. It 
follows the contract signing on 3rd June with Bretland Construction Ltd., a locally based 
Edenderry company 
The project represents a major investment in Edenderry, supported by funding of €12.2 
million under the Rural Regeneration and Development Fund (RRDF), alongside match 
funding of €3 million from Offaly County Council, demonstrating a strong partnership 
approach to regional and town centre renewal.   
This flagship regeneration project will deliver a state-of-the-art Community Library and 
Arts Space of approximately 1,800 square metres, featuring dedicated children’s, teen 
and adult library areas, study spaces, meeting rooms, a sensory space, artist studios, 
and flexible facilities for cultural and community programming.  
The development also extends beyond the building itself, incorporating outdoor 
programming areas, biodiversity-focused landscaping, accessible parking, and a new 
urban plaza. A key element of the scheme is the creation of a new pedestrian and cycle 
connection linking JKL Street to Blundell Avenue, strengthening connectivity across the 
town.

ASSOCIATION FOR CRIMINAL JUSTICE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT (ACJRD) 
ANNUAL CONFERENCE 2026 
 “PREVENTION FIRST: DESIGNING SAFER COMMUNITIES FROM SYSTEMS TO 
STREETS” 
Offaly LCSP Co-Ordinator Arlene Guilfoyle attended the ACJRD Annual Conference 2026 
in Dublin on 11th June.  This Conference was aimed at those working in government 
agencies and in the community, including policymakers, practitioners, academics, 
civil society and a wide range of disciplines that focus on all those affected by the 
Criminal Justice System.  Key themes included:  
 
SOCIAL & STRUCTURAL FOUNDATIONS  
Exploring how investment in education, housing, and healthcare can reduce the long-
term risk of offending and support resilient, thriving communities.   
 
CRIME PREVENTION THROUGH ENVIRONMENTAL DESIGN (CPTED)  
Demonstrating how well-designed spaces can naturally deter crime through principles 
such as natural surveillance, territorial reinforcement, and natural access control –-
promoting safety and positive social interaction without creating defensive or 
exclusionary environments.

SITUATIONAL CRIME PREVENTION (SCP)  
Focusing on practical, targeted measures that reduce opportunities for crime. SCP 
focuses on the "micro-level" of criminal choices, using techniques like target 
hardening (e.g., better locks and security) to increase effort and risk while limiting 
potential rewards.   
 
By bridging high-level social policy with applied environmental strategies, this 
conference sought to establish a sustainable model for safety — where prevention is 
embedded into the fabric of society, not treated as an afterthought.
